full_judgment: Facts leading to this rule, in brief, are that the petitioner was an Inspector of Food and at the relevant period was serving as a Store Keeper of the Government Flour Mill at Postagola. The petitioner was subsequently in the erstwhile East Pakistan Civil Service (Executive) and was posted as Circle Officer (Rev.), Dhamrai p. s. Dacca. Thereafter, by order of the Martial Law Administrator a departmental proceeding was drawn up by the Additional Chief Secretary of the then Government alleging inter alia that while employed as Store Keeper at the Government Flour Mill, Postagola the petitioner indulged in a benami contract business of a private firm styled as "M/s. Sonali Sangstha" whose office was situated at 74/2, Tanti Bazar, Dacca, the firm submitted a tender for appointment as Labour and Transport contractor for the Central Storage Depot at Narayangonj for the year 1966-67 and he allowed his wife to carry on business without obtaining prior permission as required under Rule 19 of the Government Servants (Conduct) Rule 1966 and as such he came within the mischief of misconduct under Rule 3(b) of the Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1960. Mr. M. Nawab, Additional Deputy Commissioner, Dacca was appointed as an enquiry officer in the said proceeding. The petitioner duly showed cause and denied the allegations made against him and asserted inter alia that his wife had started a partnership business as the shareholder with the fund obtained by transferring her property which she got from her father. He further denied that he had taken any part whatsoever in the business of the said firm nor the said firm was engaged in any business in the area over which he exercised jurisdiction. The petitioner further asserted that he was posted as a Store Keeper at Government Flour Mill at Postogola under the Directorate of Procurement and Distribution while the partnership firm submitted the tender at Narayargonj for contract under the Directorate of Movement and Storage. The petitioner thereafter received a notice from the Additional Chief Secretary to the Government along with a copy of the report of the enquiry officer to show cause why the penalty of compulsory retirement should not be imposed upon him. The petitioner again duly showed cause against the proposed penalty contending inter alia with the finding of the enquiry officer were against the evidence on record. The petitioner was thereafter served with the impugned order imposing the penalty of compulsory retirement from service with immediate effect. The petitioner applied for review of the aforesaid order to the Governor of erstwhile East Pakistan but the same was rejected. After liberation of the country he submitted a representation to the prime minister of Bangladesh but the same was also rejected. Being aggrieved the petitioner moved this court and obtained the present rule.
